label: early original-phase step after r/f/n/x tokens, in sequences starting with v or i (weak)
predicate: (phase == 0) & (t>=3) & isin(first_tok, [tok("v"), tok("i")]) & (isin(prev_tok, [tok("r"), tok("f"), tok("n"), tok("x")]) & isin(prev2_tok, [tok("r"), tok("f"), tok("n"), tok("x")]))
explanation: Sparse feature (0.013% of steps). 94% of mass is in the original phase at t=3..6 (never t<3, nearly never in copy phase beyond recall_idx 1). Strongly enriched when the sequence starts with v (16x) or i (6x) and when the previous one or two inputs are r, f, n or x (r 15x as prev_tok); the strongest examples look like v i r f [n], i r r [g], v j r r [s]. The current input token matters little. However no conjunction of these captures it well: the best predicate (first token v/i, t>=3, both previous two inputs in {r,f,n,x}) has dev precision 0.17, recall 0.42, mass recall 0.45; the feature also fires on many other prefixes containing r/f/n (e.g. c r r w, 2 r r t) and is silent on many matching ones. Appears to respond to a specific region of hidden state reached by an early v/i plus r/f-like letters rather than a describable token rule. Top-quartile activations are better covered (67%) than low ones (29%).
